newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland Protestants damage Catholic church.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland Protestants damage Catholic church.

text.p: Pro-British Protestant Loyalists broke into a Roman Catholic Church in Northern Ireland early on Sunday and broke windows before clashing with riot police, police said.
They said the incident happened at a small church in Harryville near Ballymena which has been the target of Loyalist protest every Saturday night for months.
Police said a Protestant band marched peacefully past the church on Saturday night in a weekly protest at the refusal of Catholics in the nearby village of Dunloy to allow a Protestant parade there.
But then a mob of Loyalists, so-called because of their allegiance to British rule in Northern Ireland, broke into the church and threw petrol bombs and bricks at police who dispersed them.
Police fired plastic bullets to disperse the crowd. Several officers were injured and some arrests were made, they said.
The incident highlighted communal tensions ahead of the annual "marching season" by Protestant Orange Order and other pro-British groups.
Dunloy residents have refused for months to allow the Orange Order to parade through the village, saying it is an unwelcome display of sectarian intimidation.

Last year Northern Ireland descended into the worst civil unrest for decades when police first banned and then allowed an Orange Order parade through a Catholic area of the southern town of Portadown.
Britain's new Labour government is appealing to both communities to negotiate compromise routes for the parades but efforts have so far made little headway.
